segments.title: 第84章 展信
segments.content:
To Li Luo:

You might find it strange that I'm writing to you.

I can only say that the prettier a girl is, the closer you get to her, the deeper you fall into the trap of her beauty.

I am very disappointed in you. If you hadn't joined the literature club in the end, perhaps I would have thought more highly of you.

But you were ultimately seduced by Xu Youyu into the literature club, serving as nothing more than kindling to help her become president.

Perhaps you are still feeling smug, enjoying this special treatment, immersed in the fantasy that she might like you.

Here, I can only mercilessly pop your inner bubble and tell you some cold, hard facts.

The more than two hundred words above were just the beginning.

What followed were all sorts of things about Xu Youyu, with baseless speculation about some of her actions from a conspiracy theorist's perspective, making the corners of Li Luo's mouth twitch as he read.

So this is what jealousy does to a girl's perspective on things?

The more Li Luo read, the more amused he became. He hadn't expected to find no shortage of oddballs even in a school like Fuyi High.

It's just that the direction in which these oddballs grew was a little different.

Take this letter from Qin Yawei, for instance. There were no curse words in the entire letter, yet you could feel her disgust and jealousy towards Xu Youyu in every line.

As expected of someone whose writing even Xu Youyu had to praise.

If this were his high school in his past life, he had heard of girls getting into fights, but he had never seen someone write a letter to be passive-aggressive like this.

The literature club indeed.

Li Luo hadn't seen much else, but they had certainly inherited some of the skills of scholars bickering with each other.

After reading Qin Yawei's letter, Li Luo set it aside. He then looked at the remaining three letters and picked up the one from Hua Xiuxiu.

Opening the envelope, Hua Xiuxiu's elegant handwriting spread out before him.

Class President:

The reason for writing this letter isn't to become pen pals with you. It's just that some things on my mind are perhaps easier to say this way.

I have to say thank you.

Before, I feel I was somewhat self-righteous. For the position of class president, I even secretly mocked you during the election.

Later, I discovered that you did many things that the old me couldn't have done, or even thought of.

This has changed many of my concepts and views.

So this time, during the class committee election, I did not go on stage.

I don't think I'm the best candidate in our current Class 8.

As for Li Luo being the class president, I don't think many people in the class would have a problem with it now.

But if it were me, even if I really did become the class president, I'm afraid some people would still feel I wasn't worthy.

The moment I realized this, I understood just how big the gap between you and me is in this regard.

So...

I'm very happy to continue serving as the vice president of Class 8.

For the rest of my high school career, I'll be in your care, Class President.

—Hua Xiuxiu

September 6, 2014

Li Luo: "..."

Why the hell didn't you run for it!

What's this about being won over?

After reading Hua Xiuxiu's letter, Li Luo was a bit speechless.

He hadn't expected that the reason these people didn't run for class president was that he had done too good a job before?

If I'd known, I wouldn't have been so good to you guys. You're really repaying kindness with ingratitude!

Li Luo shook his head helplessly and looked at the remaining two letters, reaching for Xu Youyu's first.

My dear little junior:

I won't just say "hello", that's too tacky.

I'm very happy you joined the literature club and contributed to me becoming president, haha.

If we're going by Qin Yawei's thoughts, she'd probably think I used some kind of honey trap.

And curse it, I still have to pay it back with a month of cleaning duty!

If you have any conscience, maybe you should reduce it a little.

Anyway, it's great to meet you. This has added a lot of fun, and appetite, to my life as a renter.

The food you make is delicious, I like it a lot.

But this is the literature club, after all. As the vice president, you still have to lead by example.

Below is my recent reading list, which I'm sharing with you.

Traditional:

Essay Collections:

Anecdotal History:

Webnovels/Entertainment:

"I'm Really Not a Star"

That's all. I don't know if there's anything you're interested in. I look forward to you sharing some of your favorite works too.

—The beautiful and confident Senior Xu Youyu

September 6, 2014

When he saw the name "I'm Really Not a Star" under the webnovel section, Li Luo covered his face and sighed.

If he hadn't been careful not to leave any clues, Li Luo would have suspected this girl was doing it on purpose.

But you and Qin Yawei really do understand each other... Li Luo laughed and shook his head, suddenly feeling the joy of corresponding by letter.

Reading a letter like this once in a while really was a different feeling from talking face-to-face.

Thinking of this, Li Luo looked at the last letter.

He wondered what Ying Chanxi had written.

Stupid idiot:

Considering that you probably don't have anyone sending you letters, I mercifully wrote this one for you. (scratch marks)

We live together, so I feel like there's not much to say in a letter.

But the thought of sitting in a Fuyi High classroom with you still feels amazing.

Just a few months ago, I thought we were about to go our separate ways.

When I found out you had started to give up on yourself, I was actually very sad.

But you gave me a surprise.

However, I hope that if there is a next time, you will still tell me clearly.

The middle school curriculum is still relatively simple, but if it were the college entrance exams, it would definitely be much better for you if I helped you review, rather than you struggling alone.

You promised me you'd get into Qianjiang University, but you only ranked in the 300s in the whole school on this placement test. You have to keep working hard.

If there's any problem you don't understand, come ask me anytime. Don't always be too proud to ask, okay? I'm number one in the grade, you know.

Also.

How do you feel about the class? Is being class president fun? Or do you really find it tiring?

If you really don't want to do it, and if it might affect your study efficiency, I think you could talk to your head teacher about it.

You have to pay attention in class too, don't daze off. You used to love chatting with Zhao Rongjun in your scratchpad during class, remember to correct that bad habit.

And um... if you feel that making a late-night snack every night is a bit tiring, but you're too embarrassed to refuse your senior's request, then you can secretly tell me, and I'll figure something out.

I know cooking is hard work. You can't wrong yourself just because you care about others' feelings.

Or you could teach me more, and I can help out more in the kitchen in the future.

Besides that, you need to go to bed earlier every day and not play on the computer too much. You promised me, otherwise I won't know how to explain it to your uncle and auntie.

You have to change and wash your sheets and quilt cover often. If you're too lazy, I'll help you take care of it when I do mine next time.

But I feel like you've matured a lot since the high school entrance exams, so you probably don't need me to worry about so much anymore.

All in all, I'm very happy that we can still be in the same high school.

In the future, I also hope we can be at the same university.

So you have to work hard!

Don't disappoint my expectations of you.

Oh right, don't you dare let anyone else see this, or I'll kill you.

—Ying Chanxi

September 6, 2014

Li Luo: "..."

This is what you meant at the beginning when you said you felt there wasn't much to say in a letter?

Out of the five letters, besides Qin Yawei's thousand-word letter of accusation, yours is the longest, okay.

(End of Chapter)
